title: Synthesis of 124I-labeled epichaperome probes and assessment in visualizing pathologic protein-protein interaction networks in tumor bearing mice
protocol: Label PU-H71 and PU-AD with iodine-124 for PET imaging.
Replace iodine in PU-H71 and PU-AD with iodine-131 for autoradiography detection.
Use labeled PU-H71 and PU-AD to detect epichaperomes at the cellular level.
Quantify epichaperome levels using PET or autoradiography probes.
Track changes in epichaperome presence over time in live patients.
Convert PU-H71 into the tin precursor PU-H71-SnMe3.
Purify PU-H71-SnMe3.
Characterize PU-H71-SnMe3.
Convert PU-AD into the tin precursor PU-AD-SnMe3.
Purify PU-AD-SnMe3.
Characterize PU-AD-SnMe3.
Weigh PU-H71 and Tris(dibenzylideneacetone)dipalladium(0) in a round-bottom flask containing a magnetic stirring bar.
Stopper the flask with a rubber septum.
Insert through the septum a syringe attached to a nitrogen-filled balloon to replace air with an inert atmosphere.
Carry out reactions in the dark.
Wrap the reaction vessel in aluminum foil.
Use an inert atmosphere during reactions.
Mix hexamethylditin in 3 mL of dry toluene.
Add the mixture through the septum using a syringe.
Place the reaction flask in an oil bath with silicone oil on a hotplate stirrer.
Stir the reaction solution at 500 rpm for 2 hours at 70°C.
Concentrate the reaction mixture using a rotary evaporator.
Dissolve the residue in 0.5 mL of CH2Cl2:MeOH (1:1) and load it onto PTLC as a uniform band.
Develop the PTLC using CH2Cl2:EtOAc:Hexane:NH3/MeOH (7N) at 2:1:2:0.5.
Scrap off the silica band containing the desired product at Rf∼0.45.
Dissolve the desired product in 50 mL of CH2Cl2:MeOH (10:1).
Filter this suspension using a sintered glass funnel.
Dry the filtrate under vacuum to afford the tin precursor molecules.
Characterize each product by NMR spectroscopy (1H NMR and 13C NMR).
Characterize each product by mass spectrometry (MS).
Dissolve 25 mg of PU-H71 in methylene chloride:methanol 1:1 v/v.
Transfer 10 μL aliquots into brown Eppendorf tubes after dissolving in 1 mL of methylene chloride:methanol 1:1 v/v.
Dry under vacuum in the Genevac for 2–3 h.
Store dried PU-H71-SnMe3 at -20°C.
Transfer 10 μL aliquots into brown Eppendorf tubes after dissolving 10 mg of PU-AD in methylene chloride:methanol 1:1 v/v.
Dry under vacuum in the Genevac for 2–3 h.
Store dried PU-AD-SnMe3 at -20°C.
Pipette 20 μL of ethanol into the brown Eppendorf tube containing 25 μg of PU-H71-SnMe3 precursor.
Pipette ≤100 μL of 124I-Sodium Iodide solution (0.5–20 mCi) into the vial.
Pipette 5 μL of chloramine-T solution (2 mg/mL in acetic acid) into the vial.
Incubate the reaction mixture for 5 min at 24 ± 2°C.
Centrifuge the samples in a minifuge for 15 s at approximately 12 × g.
Assay the amount of activity in the reaction vial by placing it in the dose calibrator chamber.
Select iodine-124 as the radionuclide in the isotope selector.
Pre-condition the C18 cartridge with 10 mL of ethanol followed by 10 mL water.
Draw 1 mL of water from a syringe into the reaction mixture.
Mix the water and reaction mixture in the syringe thoroughly.
Load the mixed reaction mixture onto a preconditioned C18 cartridge.
Elute radioactive iodine with 10 mL of water.
Discard the eluted water as radioactive waste.
Rinse the C18 cartridge with an additional 10 mL of water.
Discard the rinse water as radioactive waste.
Use ≤3 mL of ethanol to elute the product from the C18 Sep-Pak into individual Eppendorf tubes.
Record the activity and time of the eluted fractions.
Elute the compound in 0.3 mL fractions, combining those with highest activities.
Reduce ethanol volume to approximately 0.1–0.3 mL at ≤45°C using inert gas flow.
Regulate the inert gas flow rate to <100 mL/min to prevent spilling and loss of radioactivity.
Do not completely dry the solvent; retain enough for redissolving without requiring excessive volumes.
Formulate the reaction mixture in 1–10 mL of saline.
Pass the reaction mixture through a 0.2 μm sterile filter into the final product vial.
Remove 0.05 mL of the final product using sterile and pyrogen-free pipettes or tuberculin syringe for QC test.
Prepare [124I]-PU-H71 for analysis and characterization.
Use HPLC to determine the retention time of the radioactive sample.
Match the retention time of the radioactive sample with a non-radioactive standard.
Evaluate the purity percentage of the radiolabeled probe using the area under the curve in the HPLC chromatogram.
Formulate the radiolabeled compound in saline and/or buffered solution for administration.
Ensure that ethanol concentration, if used as an excipient, does not exceed 5% v/v in the solution.
Use gas chromatography to determine residual solvent content in the formulation.
Perform visual inspection to ensure the injectable is clear and free of particles.
Prepare the blank solution by adding 0.6 mL of ethanol to a 10 mL vial of saline.
Run the PU-H71 analytical sequence using isocratic condition (28% acetonitrile/ 72% water with added 0.1% TFA).
Inject 20 μL of blank solution.
Inject 20 μL of reference standard solution.
Inject 20 μL of blank solution.
Inject 20 μL of [124I]-PU-H71.
Measure the pH by taking 2 μL of final formulation and dropping it onto a pH paper.
Ensure the pH is between 5.5 and 8.0 for the radiopharmaceutical.
Use the trypan blue dye exclusion method to count viable cells.
Calculate the number of MDA-MB-468 cells needed per well for optimal growth to achieve 70% confluence in 2 mL of media.
Combine calculated cell numbers in a single 50 mL Falcon tube before distributing to respective wells.
Treat cells with vehicle, 1 μM PU-AD, and 1 μM PU-H71 in triplicates.
Add 2 μL of the 10 mM stock solution of PU-H71 or PU-AD to each well containing 2 mL of media.
Incubate cells treated with [124I]-PU-AD at a concentration of 18.5–37 kBq per well for 1 hour at 37°C.
Add the same amount of sample in separate Eppendorf tubes as controls for total activity measurement.
Aspirate media from the wells in 6-well plates.
Wash cells three times with cold 1× PBS.
Detach cells using 0.25% trypsin for 5 minutes.
Collect detached cells into Eppendorf tubes.
Measure radioactivity associated with each experimental condition using a gamma counter.
Record raw values in CPM (counts per minute) for each sample.
Measure the radioactivity in controls.
Divide the CPM values from each sample by the CPM values from the control.
Multiply the result by 100 to obtain % uptake normalized to each experimental condition.
Inject radiolabeled epichaperome probe via tail vein.
Administer anesthesia to the animal.
Perform PET imaging starting 1 hour post injection and continue up to 72 hours as needed.
Label mouse cages with radioactive cage cards.
Add 0.01% potassium iodide solution to the drinking water starting 48 hours before tracer administration.
Inject intravenously via the tail vein using a 1.0 mL insulin syringe, 5.55–9.25 MBq (150–250 mCi) of [124I]-PU-H71 or [124I]-PU-AD in 200 μL of 5% ethanol in saline.
Place the mouse under a heat lamp for 2–4 minutes and rub the area with an alcohol swab to induce vasodilation before injection.
Pull the syringe’s plunger outward to observe blood flow if necessary to confirm needle placement in the tail vein.
Apply mild pressure at the injection site with a sterile alcohol wipe for 5–15 seconds if minor bleeding occurs after withdrawal of the syringe.
Wipe the tail clean using a sterile alcohol wipe after the injection.
Remark tail markings as necessary if used for mouse identification.
Place the animal in an induction chamber for anesthesia using 2% isoflurane in oxygen at a flow rate of 2 L/min at designated time points post probe administration.
Prepare the PET scanner.
Create a new file in the MicroPET 2.0 program with acquisition time parameters set to 10 minutes for early time points and 20 minutes for later time points.
Input the necessary information regarding the mouse, including the administered radioactive dose, physical half-life of 124I, remaining activity in the used syringe, and measurement time point.
Place the animal at the center of the field of view of the PET scanner.
Position the mouse in a prone and headfirst orientation.
Maintain the animal under 2% isoflurane anesthesia during the entire scanning period.
Initiate a 30-minute PET scan.
Obtain list-mode data for each animal to acquire a minimum of 5 million coincident counts.
Use an energy window of 420–580 keV and a coincidence timing window of 6 ns.
Remove the mouse from the scanner once the acquisition is finished.
Return the mouse to its cage, which should display a radioactive cage card.
Dispose of bedding, cage, food, water, waste as radioactive waste separately.
Sort the resulting list-mode data into 2-dimensional histograms by Fourier rebinding.
Reconstruct transverse images by filtered back projection (FBP).
Correct the image data for dead-time count losses.
Correct the image data for physical decay to the time of injection.
Perform ROI analysis of the reconstructed images using ASIPro VMTM (Siemens Medical Solutions, USA).
Record the maximum pixel value for each tissue/organ ROI.
Reconstruct microPET images including 124I images.

Quantitate images by parameterizing them in terms of activity concentration using a system calibration factor derived from reconstructed images of a mouse-sized water-filled cylinder containing known concentrations of 18F.
Convert the 18F calibration factor to the 124I calibration factor by adjusting for the difference in positron branching ratio between 18F and 124I.
Normalize image data to the administered activity to parameterize microPET images in terms of %ID/g, corrected for decay of 124I to the time of injection.
Apply post-reconstruction smoothing to improve image quality if necessary.
